concepts.label: Transcoder (non-JSON document encode/decode)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused from documents.json (extracted earlier in this same batch), which named the concept via its own link to this page ('using a [transcoder](nonjson.md)'). This page is the transcoder's own full first-hand definition: 'if your application requires a non-JSON format... you can write a _transcoder_ which handles the encoding and decoding of your documents to and from the server.'

concepts.label: Common flags (32-bit item metadata field encoding JSON/UTF-8/RAW/PRIVATE format)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept covers this specific item-metadata mechanism. Distinct from data:item (the general item/metadata concept) in that this is specifically the type-code field a transcoder writes/reads to know how to (de)serialize.

concepts.label: SQL++
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - named directly as one of the two access surfaces non-JSON serialization breaks.

concepts.label: MapReduce Views from the Java SDK
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - round 3's howtos/view-queries-with-sdk.json id; this page states non-JSON documents have only 'limited support' for MapReduce views, as against no support at all for Query/Search.

concepts.label: Full Text Search (capability)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - named directly as an access surface unavailable to non-JSON documents.

relations.subject: sdk:transcoder
relations.evidence: When the SDK serializes the Document, it notes the type of serialization performed (JSON) and sends a corresponding type code along with the serialized document to the server to be stored. This type code is stored in the flags field within the item's metadata.

relations.subject: sdk:transcoder
relations.evidence: Note that only JSON documents can be accessed using Query and Search.

relations.subject: sdk:transcoder
relations.evidence: Limited support for non-JSON documents is available for MapReduce views.

notable_absence.finding: The page states non-JSON documents are inaccessible via the Web UI too ('non-JSON documents will not be accessible using the Web UI (the contents will be shown in their Base64 equivalent)') but this is a degraded-view case, not a clean doesNotSupport boundary like Query/Search - the content is still shown, just Base64-encoded. Recorded here rather than forcing it into a relation that would overstate the constraint.

cross_component_finding: This page fills in the concept (sdk:transcoder, sdk:common-flags) that documents.json - extracted earlier in this same batch - could only name via a forward link, confirming the round's expectation that concept-docs pages sometimes supply the first full-content definition for a concept another concept-docs page in the same tree already had to reference. No howto page in rounds 3/4 touched transcoders or common flags at all, so both ids are new to the corpus.
